# What Is Supply Chain Performance Management (SCPM)?


By[Jacqueline Nance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/jacqueline-nance) , *Sr. Content Marketing Manager*


Last Updated August 19, 2026


7 min read


In this article, learn about:


-


What supply chain performance management is and where it fits


-


Which supplier performance metrics retailers track


-


Why early visibility into supplier performance matters


---


Retailers depend on suppliers to get the right products to the right place at the right time. When that starts to break down, the signs usually show up in the data: orders arriving short, shipments running late, ASNs that do not match what was delivered, or pesky lead times that keep moving in the wrong direction.


Supply chain performance management (SCPM) puts those signals in one place, so retailers and suppliers can see what is happening and address it earlier. Instead of waiting for a quarterly review or a string of stockouts to confirm there's a problem, teams can track performance as it changes and focus on the areas that need attention.


At its core, SCPM is about making supplier performance easier to see, discuss, and improve. The better that visibility is, the easier it becomes to keep inventory moving and to prevent small problems from becoming expensive ones.


## What Is Supply Chain Performance Management?


The[Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals](https://cscmp.org/) defines supply chain management as the function that links a company's major business processes into one working model. That includes coordination with other companies in the chain, from suppliers to intermediaries to distributors. SCPM tells a retailer whether that coordination is actually happening, shipment by shipment.


## Where Does SCPM Fit Within Supply Chain Management?


[ASCM's SCOR Digital Standard](https://www.ascm.org/corporate-solutions/standards-tools/scor-ds/) is the supply chain field's most widely used process framework. Its most recent update added an "Orchestrate" stage to cover strategy, technology, and performance management.


## Why Does Supply Chain Performance Management Matter Now?


In 2025,retail supply chains experienced two disruptions at once. NRF and Kantar's[2026 Top 50 Global Retailers analysis](https://nrf.com/research-insights/top-retailers/top-50-global-retailers/top-50-global-retailers-2026) points to U.S. policy shifts and fast-changing tariffs forcing manufacturers and retailers into repeated strategic pivots. On top of that volatility, the same analysis notes a surge in cybercrime targeting logistics and procurement systems, adding a new failure point on top of the usual cargo theft and in-store shrink retailers already track.


When unit costs and delivery reliability are both under pressure at the same time, the retailers with earlier visibility into which supplier relationships are underperforming are the ones who can act before a stockout or a chargeback dispute happens. That is the practical argument for supply chain performance management: It is not about proving a supplier wrong, but rather is about seeing a problem multiple shipments before it becomes an empty shelf instead of finding out when the shelf is already empty.


## What Metrics Does Supply Chain Performance Management Track?


Most supplier performance programs focus on a core set of metrics that show whether orders are arriving complete, accurate, and on schedule:


-


[On-time, in-full delivery (OTIF)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/walmart-otif-fundamentals) **:** Whether an order arrives within the expected delivery window and in the quantity ordered


-


**Fill rate:** The percentage of an order a supplier fulfills


-


**Advance Ship Notice (ASN) accuracy:** Whether the shipment data sent electronically matches what physically arrives


-


**Lead time:** The time between order placement and delivery


Looking at these metrics together gives retailers a clearer view of supplier performance and where problems may be developing.


**Metric**


**What it can signal**


**If the issue continues**


**OTIF**


Orders are consistently arriving late or incomplete


Inventory falls below plan, increasing stockout risk


**Fill rate**


Suppliers are unable to fulfill the quantities ordered


Replenishment becomes less reliable and shelf availability suffers


**ASN accuracy**


Shipment data doesn't match what physically arrives


Receiving slows, inventory records become unreliable, and deductions may follow


**Lead time**


Orders are taking longer to fulfill than expected


Reorder assumptions become inaccurate and safety stock gets consumed


## Turning Performance Metrics Into Action


Tracking these metrics is only useful if they lead somewhere. When OTIF declines, teams should be able to isolate whether the problem is concentrated by supplier, item, distribution center, carrier, or delivery lane.


If ASN accuracy drops, teams should be able to determine whether the issue is bad source data, an EDI failure, or a warehouse execution problem. SCPM gives both trading partners the visibility and process to find the cause, assign ownership, and determine whether the fix worked.


**Related Reading:**[How To Build an Effective Supplier Scorecard](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-build-an-effective-supplier-scorecard)


## How Is SCPM Different From a Supplier Scorecard?


Most retailers already use some form of supplier scorecard. The limitation is often timing: A quarterly scorecard shows what happened, but it may come too late to influence the next shipment.


SCPM keeps that view current using the order, shipment, and[EDI data](https://www.spscommerce.com/what-is-edi/) retailers and suppliers already exchange. Instead of relying on past incidents, both sides can work from the same metrics, spot changes in performance, and address issues as they develop.


That shared visibility is the key difference. A periodic scorecard can feel like a report card. SCPM turns performance data into a shared operating picture that can be used to to improve what happens next.


**Related Reading:**[A Collaborative Approach to Supplier Performance Management](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/collaborative-vendor-scorecarding-spse)


## What Does Supply Chain Performance Management Look Like in Practice?


For Burlington, supplier performance problems had a direct operational cost. Incorrect packing, late shipments, damaged goods, and other vendor errors had to be pulled from the normal distribution center flow and handled separately, requiring additional labor, space, and resources.


[Burlington's experience](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/burlington-case-study/) shows what stronger supplier performance visibility can look like in practice. By bringing performance data together, the retailer was better able to identify routing, shipping, and packaging issues and communicate those findings to suppliers.


Burlington eliminated 63% of problem shipments, reduced distribution center cycle time by more than 40%, improved DC productivity by 14%, and lowered distribution cost per unit by 8%. More importantly, the data gave Burlington and its vendors a clearer view of where problems were occurring so they could address the issues behind them.


## How Do Retailers Build Continuous Supplier Performance Management?


Tracking supplier performance only matters if teams act on what the data shows. When a metric slips, retailers and suppliers should be able to identify the cause, assign ownership, and determine whether the fix improves performance.


That requires an ongoing operating rhythm rather than an annual review. Reviewing performance consistently gives both sides a chance to correct problems before they become stockouts, deductions, or larger disruptions.


## Supply Chain Performance Management FAQs


### What does SCPM stand for?


SCPM stands for supply chain performance management, the ongoing measurement of how well a supplier is executing against agreed metrics like on-time delivery, fill rate, and shipment accuracy.


### How is supply chain performance management different from a vendor scorecard?


A vendor scorecard is often a static, periodic report. Supply chain performance management is the broader, continuous discipline that a modern scorecard is one output of: the underlying data, the cadence it updates on, and the shared visibility both retailer and supplier have into it.


### What metrics does SCPM track?


Most programs center on a small set of metrics: OTIF, fill rate, ASN accuracy, and lead time. Retailers often add category or supplier-specific metrics on top of that core set.


### Who typically owns supply chain performance management at a retailer?


Ownership usually sits with operations, merchandising, or vendor compliance leadership, since the metrics touch inventory availability, supplier relationships, and margin protection at once. Larger organizations often build cross-functional review into the process rather than housing it in a single department.
